question: According to the design paper describing the Dog Aging Project as an open-data, community-science longitudinal study of ageing in companion dogs, which categories of data does the project plan to collect?
answer: Survey data, environmental information, electronic veterinary medical records, genome-wide sequence information, clinicopathology, and molecular phenotypes derived from blood cells, plasma and faecal samples.

evidence.title: An open science study of ageing in companion dogs.
evidence.quote: To take advantage of this opportunity, the Dog Aging Project will collect extensive survey data, environmental information, electronic veterinary medical records, genome-wide sequence information, clinicopathology and molecular phenotypes derived from blood cells, plasma and faecal samples.

question: In the Dog Aging Project precision cohort, one thousand dog-owner pairs were recruited into cohort strata. On which four variables were those strata based?
answer: Life stage, sex, size, and geography.

evidence.title: Rationale and design of the Dog Aging Project precision cohort: a multi-omic resource for longitudinal research in geroscience.
evidence.quote: One thousand dog-owner pairs were recruited into cohort strata based on life stage, sex, size, and geography.

question: In the cross-sectional analysis of 40,367 initial Dog Aging Project survey responses (2020-2022) on owner dietary choices, what percentage of owners fed a commercially prepared extruded dry diet (kibble) as their dog's primary diet component?

evidence.title: Dog and owner demographics impact dietary choices in Dog Aging Project cohort.
evidence.quote: Most owners (82%) fed a commercially prepared extruded dry diet (kibble) as the primary diet component.

question: The Test of Rapamycin in Aging Dogs (TRIAD) recruits dogs from Dog Aging Project participants. What is its trial design, and in which dogs does it test rapamycin?
answer: A parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial testing whether rapamycin prolongs lifespan and improves healthspan metrics in healthy, middle-aged dogs.

evidence.title: Test of Rapamycin in Aging Dogs (TRIAD): study design and rationale for a prospective, parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial of rapamycin in healthy middle-aged dogs from the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: The Test of Rapamycin In Aging Dogs (TRIAD) randomized clinical trial is a parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial that will test the ability of rapamycin to prolong lifespan and improve several healthspan metrics in healthy, middle-aged dogs recruited from Dog Aging Project participants.

question: In the Dog Aging Project analysis of owner-reported supplement use from enrollment surveys collected 2020-2022, what proportion of the 40,367 dogs received supplements, and which two supplement types were most common among supplemented dogs?
answer: 52% (20,993 of 40,367) received supplements; the most common were omega-3 fatty acids (57%) and joint supplements (56%).

evidence.title: Supplement use is common in Dog Aging Project participants, especially among dogs with orthopedic conditions, and varies by life stage.
evidence.quote: Half of the dogs in this study (20,993 of 40,367 [52%]) received supplements. Of those receiving supplements, the most common supplements administered were omega-3 fatty acids (11,934 [57%]) and joint supplements (11,810 [56%]).

question: In the validation of the Dog Aging Project End of Life Survey (EOLS), inter-rater reliability was assessed for three themes. Which theme had the highest reliability, and what were the kappa values for all three?
answer: Cause of death was highest (κ = 0.73); perimortem quality of life κ = 0.49; reason for euthanasia κ = 0.3.

evidence.title: Development and validation of a novel instrument to capture companion dog mortality data: the Dog Aging Project End of Life Survey.
evidence.quote: The EOLS had fair to substantial reliability for the 3 validation themes-cause of death (κ = 0.73; 95% CI, 0.5 to 0.95), perimortem quality of life (κ = 0.49; 95% CI, 0.26 to 0.73), and reason for euthanasia (κ = 0.3; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.52)-and had no need for any substantial content alterations based on free-text analysis.

question: In the Dog Aging Project study comparing owner-reported diagnoses from the Health and Life Experience Survey with veterinary electronic medical records across 20 disease categories, which category had the lowest agreement and which had the highest, with their agreement percentages?
answer: Lowest: dental/oral at 44%. Highest: endocrine, immune, and "other" categories at 99%.

evidence.title: Accuracy of owner-reported diagnoses for dogs enrolled in the Dog Aging Project as compared to veterinary electronic medical records.
evidence.quote: Agreement was highest in endocrine, immune, and "other" categories (99%) and lowest in dental/oral (44%).

question: The Dog Aging Project precision cohort recruited one thousand dog-owner pairs for multi-omic profiling. From how many dogs did the project actually collect and process blood, urine, fecal, and hair samples in collaboration with primary care veterinarians?

evidence.title: Rationale and design of the Dog Aging Project precision cohort: a multi-omic resource for longitudinal research in geroscience.
evidence.quote: In collaboration with primary care veterinarians, we collected and processed blood, urine, fecal, and hair samples from 976 dogs.

evidence.title: Protein Catabolites as Blood-Based Biomarkers of Aging Physiology: Findings From the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: Beginning in January of 2021, 976 dogs were recruited into the Precision Cohort, representing a wide diversity of dog age, genetics, and geography.

notes: Second evidence item corroborates the 976 figure from the first-year metabolome analysis of the same cohort.

question: In the Dog Aging Project comparison of owner-reported breed ancestry with genetic breed results for 5,673 dogs, what percentage of owners identified their dog's breed as matching the genetic report, and what was the most common explanation among owners who reported disagreement?
answer: 80% matched; among those disagreeing, most had dogs of a breed not included in the genetic reference panel.

evidence.title: Comparing owner reported and genetic breed identification reveals high concordance in a large cohort from the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: We find that 80% of dog owners identified their dog's breed as matching the genetic reports. Among those few who reported disagreement with the genetic results, the majority indicated having dogs belonging to a breed not included in the reference panel.

question: In the retrospective analysis of Dog Aging Project End of Life Survey responses from 2020 through 2024, what proportion of owners reported pain and/or suffering as a reason for euthanasia, and what was the odds ratio associating recent veterinary consultation with reporting pain or suffering?
answer: 87% (7,764 of 8,955 owners); recent veterinary consultation OR 1.76 (95% CI 1.50-2.05).

evidence.title: Poor quality of life and recent veterinary consultation are associated with increased owner-perceived pain and/or suffering prior to euthanasia in dogs.
evidence.quote: Overall, 7,764 of 8,955 owners (87%) reported pain and/or suffering as a reason for euthanasia, with older owners, smaller dogs, and dogs < 5 years of age as factors that had lower frequency of pain as a reason for euthanasia.

evidence.title: Poor quality of life and recent veterinary consultation are associated with increased owner-perceived pain and/or suffering prior to euthanasia in dogs.
evidence.quote: Recent veterinary consultation was positively associated with pain or suffering (OR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.50 to 2.05), and better quality of life was negatively associated with pain or suffering (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86 to 0.93).

question: In the Dog Aging Project study comparing owner-reported HLES diagnoses with veterinary electronic medical records, how was the sample of 350 dogs composed with respect to the five target disease categories, and why were 50 dogs added above the 300-dog target from the power analysis?
answer: 250 dogs with at least one target-disease-category diagnosis plus 100 dogs with none; the extra 50 allowed for an anticipated 16% dropout due to incomplete records.

evidence.title: Accuracy of owner-reported diagnoses for dogs enrolled in the Dog Aging Project as compared to veterinary electronic medical records.
evidence.quote: Our analysis suggested that a sample of 300 dogs would yield 90% power to detect whether HLES reports of dogs with no diseases in the TDCs matched VEMR records with no diseases in the TDCs better than expected by chance. Thus, to adequately assess agreement between VEMR data and the owner-reported HLES for the five TDCs, a total study sample of 350 dogs was randomly selected from among those eligible – 250 dogs with a minimum of one TDC diagnosis and 100 dogs without a TDC diagnosis – with the additional 50 above the 300-dog target included to account for an anticipated 16% dropout rate due to incomplete records.

question: In the second pilot validating the Dog Aging Project chronic diagnosis inventory (CDI) for documenting canine multimorbidity, which indexed condition was the only one whose inter-rater agreement was worse than chance, and what was its kappa?

evidence.title: Development and validation of a chronic diagnosis inventory that enables reliable documentation of canine multimorbidity in the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: Periodontal disease was the only condition with inter-rater agreement worse than chance agreement (κ = −0.24; *P* = .31).

question: In the Dog Aging Project analysis of owner-reported supplement use, how did the proportion of dogs receiving supplements change across owner-perceived overall health, from dogs rated in excellent health to those rated in very poor health?
answer: It rose from 45% among dogs in excellent health to 68% among dogs in very poor health.

evidence.title: Supplement use is common in Dog Aging Project participants, especially among dogs with orthopedic conditions, and varies by life stage.
evidence.quote: Dogs reported to be in poorer overall health were more likely to receive supplements compared to their counterparts reported to be in better health, with supplement use increasing from 45% among dogs in excellent health to 68% for those in very poor health.
